security_audit.summary: All 264 static alerts concern documentation, defensive checks, or intended publishing operations rather than demonstrated threats. No evidence found of credential theft or audit-directed prompt injection. Directory packaging can publish unintended content if a concurrent writer replaces selected paths after symlink checks.

remediation.issue: Directory packaging checks file types before a separate ZIP process reopens mutable source paths.
remediation.suggestion: Snapshot selected files through descriptor-relative, no-follow opens into a private staging directory. Reject unsafe ancestors and file types, then archive only the snapshot.

semantic_findings.title: Source Replacement Can Bypass Directory Symlink Filtering
semantic_findings.description: Collection rejects symlinks, but ZIP creation later reopens paths and follows links. A concurrent writer could replace a selected file or ancestor directory with a symlink to outside data. Name-only verification would accept the substituted contents, potentially publishing unintended files without a sensitive-name warning.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The lstat checks and ZIP reads occur separately without descriptor-bound copying or file-identity verification. Exploitation requires concurrent write access to the selected source tree.

content.user_title: Publish Files and Static Sites to Brewpage
content.value_statement: Sharing a report or static demo often requires a hosting setup. This skill uploads selected content to brewpage.app and returns a shareable link.
actual_capabilities: Publish text and Markdown through the HTML endpoint, validate JSON payloads, and upload individual files.
Package built static directories with relative paths, extension filtering, and archive integrity checks.
Inspect supplied ZIP archives and require digest-bound approval for unexpected or sensitive filenames.
Request explicit namespace and password choices, plus optional retention, entry file, and delivery mode settings.
Save returned owner tokens and publication metadata in private project history with Git exclusion checks.
Query current service limits and return the exact server link with relevant notices.
limitations: Requires network access and POSIX tools, including Bash, curl, jq, and Python. Site uploads also require Node.js and archive utilities.
Does not build application sources or run backend services. Site uploads require prepared static output.
Filename filtering does not detect embedded secrets. Concurrent source changes can undermine directory symlink filtering.
Publications expire and remain subject to service limits. An unlisted namespace alone does not restrict reader access.

use_cases.title: Share Release Notes
use_cases.description: Publish approved Markdown release notes with a short retention period and a reader link.

use_cases.title: Preview a Static Demo
use_cases.description: Upload a prepared build directory, choose its entry page, and share the returned site URL for review.

use_cases.title: Distribute a Temporary Report
use_cases.description: Share an approved PDF using an unlisted namespace and optional password protection from an existing local password file.

prompt_templates.title: Publish a Short Note
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish this note to brewpage.app: [approved text]. Ask me to choose the namespace and password option before uploading.

prompt_templates.title: Share a Report File
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish [report path] with a one-day TTL. Show its size and type, then ask for my namespace and password choices.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy Built Static Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish the stable build directory [path] with entry [page.html] and a seven-day TTL. Show upload details and request namespace and password choices.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Site Archive
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [site.zip] for publication. Ask for namespace and password choices. If flagged, show the manifest and digest, then await my approval.

output_examples.input: Publish an approved release note without a password.
output: Owner token saved to private project history.
The unlisted link can be opened by anyone who has it.

output_examples.input: Publish a ZIP containing a filename marked as sensitive.
output: Review the archive manifest, flagged filenames, and SHA256 digest.
Approve the reviewed archive or cancel.

output_examples.input: Publish a directory without an HTML entry page.
output_examples.output: Publication stopped because no HTML entry page was found. Build the static site first and select its output directory.

best_practices: Review file contents for secrets and publish only stable, approved build output.
Choose public visibility deliberately. Use password protection when an unlisted link is insufficient.
Keep owner-token history private and preserve the exact returned URL and expiry metadata.
anti_patterns: Publishing source trees, credentials, personal data, or mutable build directories without review.
Treating an unlisted namespace as authentication or ignoring publication expiry.
Pasting password contents or owner tokens into conversations, or approving a digest without reviewing its manifest.

faq.question: What content can I publish?
faq.answer: You can publish text, Markdown, JSON, individual files, built static directories, and supported ZIP site archives.

faq.question: Do I need an account?
faq.answer: No account is required for publishing. Optional account features depend on the hosting service.

faq.question: Is an unlisted namespace private?
faq.answer: It is not listed publicly, but anyone with the link can open it unless password protection restricts access.

faq.question: How are passwords supplied?
faq.answer: Provide the absolute path to an existing password file. The script validates it and uses private header files for transport.

faq.question: Where are owner tokens stored?
faq.answer: Tokens are stored in .claude/brewpage-history.md at the project root. History uses mode 600 and Git exclusion checks; tokens are not printed in chat.

faq.question: How long do publications last?
faq.answer: The default requested TTL is 15 days. Service limits apply, and returned expiry metadata determines actual retention.
